basis_statement: Every height in this base is what DDA PERMITS on the parcel, not what is standing on it. MAX_HEIGHT_FLOORS is a ceiling. A completed plot may be built well below it, and an empty plot carries a permitted height with nothing on it at all. CONSTRUCTION_STATUS is carried through per feature so the two can be told apart downstream, but it does not change the height -- it only says whether anything is there.
axis_convention: Baked rings are a local PLAN frame in metres: x = easting - origin.x, y = northing - origin.y. The renderer supplies the Y-up step with rotateX(-PI/2), which is the same one-line move packages/engine/solum_massing/solid.py -> web/src/components/Scene.tsx already makes. Keeping the bake in plan means a district and a plot study cannot end up mirrored against each other.

vertical.basis: No DEM is sampled at LOD1. This AOI spans 1.6 km of Dubai coastal plain, where terrain relief is a small fraction of one storey, and the global fallback (Copernicus GLO-30) is a DSM -- it contains the buildings themselves, so sampling it to seat buildings would double-count them. A flat plane at a documented, unknown datum is the honest LOD1 statement. Revisit only with a bare-earth DTM, and only if a use case needs it.

height_chain: MAX_HEIGHT_METERS  -> authority, metres published for this plot
HEIGHT_CATEGORY    -> assumption, storey band midpoint x floor_height_m
(nothing)          -> unavailable, drawn as a ground outline, never as an invented building

sources.name: Dubai Development Authority BASIC_LAND_BASE parcel layer
sources.coverage: DDA governs 44.8% of Dubai's 3,039 registered projects (measured 2026-08-29 against the RERA register). Trakhees 30.4%, Dubai Municipality 18.1%, Dubai South 4.2%, DSO 2.4%. An AOI that straddles a jurisdiction boundary will simply return fewer parcels there -- that gap is reported, not filled.

sources.name: Esri World Imagery tile cache
sources.note: Already wired through packages/engine/solum_massing/basemap.py. Esri's terms require the source named wherever the imagery is shown.

sources.name: OpenStreetMap building footprints (via Overpass)
sources.coverage: 471 footprints inside this AOI; 28 carry a surveyed height (20 building:levels, 8 height). Community-surveyed, so completeness varies street by street and nothing here treats an OSM height as authoritative.

sources.note: The only source in this base delivered in WGS84. It is reprojected once, offline, into EPSG:3997 so that no downstream geometry mixes degrees with metres.
